question: How to improve site safety when using robotics?

answer.answer:
The single route the literature gives to improved site safety (VA13) is prefabrication and off-site work (PR2): move the task into the factory and the exposure on site goes with it. That route is not a machine purchase, it is bought upstream with design for manufacture and assembly (PR9), early contractor involvement (CO11) and supply chain integration (VA14), and it carries its own burdens: prefabrication relies on precise up-front planning (RI14) and on regulatory compliance and certification (RI18). Where work must stay on site, the safety mechanism on record is collaborative human-robot interaction (CO6) operating within force limits, which reduces the work safety concern (RI20) rather than delivering the site safety value directly, and which itself depends on workforce training (RI6) and on robot safety standards (RI18). Note the gap: 39 of the 50 coded cases pursue site safety, but only 12 carry the prefabrication path that the literature offers for it, so most safety gains in the record are not explained by any cited mechanism.

**The one cited path into VA13**

VA13 "Improve site safety" is a Value [1], applying in the Structural Construction phase in a value-realizing role [2]. It carries exactly 1 inbound and 0 outbound dependency edges, and 39 of the 50 coded cases draw on it. [3] That single edge is DEP19, PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site" enablesCapability VA13, backed by peer-reviewed evidence and carried by 12 of the 50 coded cases: moving work offsite improves site safety [3]. So of the 39 cases seeking the value, only 12 carry both ends of the one path the literature asserts to it.

**What prefabrication requires, and what it costs**

20 of the 50 cases draw on PR2 [3]. Its cited upstream conditions differ in how widely they are carried: DfMA for DFAB process (PR9) enablesCapability PR2, carried by 15 of the 50 [3]; Early contractor involvement (CO11) enablesCapability PR2, carried by 13, on the reasoning that the delivering production party must be in the early design phase [3]; Integrate supply chain (VA14) enablesCapability PR2, carried by 12 [3]. Against that, PR2 imposes: it dependsOn RI14 "Rely on precise planning", carried by 18 of the 50 [3], and it dependsOn RI18 "Regulatory/legal concern", carried by 10, where offsite compliance requires third-party certification and traceability [3]. If robotic assembly is the target, PR4 "Robotic assembly" hasPrecondition PR2, carried by 4 of the 50: automated overhead delivery and assembly requires extensive prefabrication and unification of materials [3]. Alongside safety, the same prefabrication node also feeds VA2 "Reduce time/improve productivity/efficiency" (carried by 19) [3], VA3 "Improve quality/performance" (18) [3] and VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints" (14) [3], so the safety edge is the least-carried of PR2's four value outputs.

**On-site work: the collaborative-operation route**

DEP57 has CO6 "Human-robot interaction" mitigates RI20 "Work safety concern", on standards evidence, carried by 4 of the 50: power-and-force-limiting collaborative operation within biomechanical limits mitigates contact-injury risk. [3] This is one step away from VA13, since its far end is the risk RI20, not the value. RI20 is drawn on by 13 of the 50 and carries 3 cited edges in total, of which only this one is in front of me [3], so I cannot say how many routes reach it. CO6's own preconditions are unequal: it dependsOn RI6 "Require workforce training", carried by 27 of the 50, because human-robot collaboration is contingent on a skilled workforce [3], while it dependsOn RI18 "Regulatory/legal concern" on robot safety standards evidence, carried by only 2 [3]. 32 of the 50 cases draw on CO6 [3] and 44 of the 50 draw on RI6 [3]; training is the most widely present item in this whole answer, and VA13 and RI6 co-occur in 36 cases [3], which is correlation, not an asserted mechanism.

**Levers the literature has not connected**

Several safety-relevant enablers carry no cited edge at all, which means the evidence for them is case frequency and co-occurrence only. CO8 "Remote-control" is drawn on by 18 of the 50 and carries no dependency edges [3]; VA25 "Reduce disruption due to hazards" by 13, likewise edgeless [3]; RI9 "Rely on digital system" by 39, edgeless [3]; PR15 "Robotic pickup/selection" by 19 [3] and PR19 "Robotic drilling" by 9 [3], both edgeless. PR15 co-occurs with VA13 at weight 18 [4] and CO6 co-occurs with VA13 at weight 28 [5], again correlation. The cited layer covers only 68 of the 140 enablers, and 60% of Risks and 48% of Values carry no edge [3], so silence here is a property of the literature, not a verdict on the lever.

**Deployed records**

Three deployed processes in this context name safety as the adoption motive, and none of them is a prefabrication case: census_RXM4-5, adopted to address safety and labor, performs digging and material handling on sitework, substructure and foundation, at technology readiness level 8 [6]; census_RXM1-3, adopted to address safety and market, performs digging and material handling on sitework, at technology readiness level 8 [7]; census_RXM23-1, adopted to address safety, performs drilling on the structural core and sitework, at technology readiness level 7 [8]. The context gives no firm for any of the three, and it does not link them to specific enablers, so I cannot say which of VA13, CO6 or PR2 they exhibit. What they do show is that the deployed safety motive in this material sits on in-situ earthmoving, handling and drilling, the opposite of the off-site path that carries the only cited edge to VA13.

**Two things to watch on site**

RI5 "Location dependent/site constraint" constrains PR12 "Path-planning", carried by 15 of the 50, because reliable GNSS is typically unavailable indoors and that constrains the localisation method [3], a direct operational hazard for any mobile machine working inside a structure. And for on-site fabrication, AT9 "Mobile" enablesCapability PR8 "On-site DFAB", carried by 9 of the 50, via autonomous repositioning and localisation [3], which keeps the work, and the exposure, on site rather than removing it.
